segments.text: I wonder how much of the meetings is talking about the stuff of the meetings.
Yeah, exactly, yeah, yeah, yeah.
I don't really start that.
Welcome, sir.
Okay.
All right.
So, shall we talk about it?
Or shall we just go around and everyone says what they, what they've been doing?
Has anybody done anything?
No one.
Well, I am sorry.
Yeah.
Sounds like you've done something.
Sorry.
Okay, well, I've got a browser now, which, whoops, I'll run it up.
Whoops, there.
Oh, I got mine as well.
Look at this.
It smells like a good start.
Okay.
Yeah.

So, yeah, we've got a browser with, um, which comes up automatically with the transcription box and the topics, and then when you go on the menu, you can select the summarization box, which pops up, and an audio player.
Right.

Um, and I, I think the search works as well, so you pop up a search, and it loads up, um, just the background window, so empty, and, um, so when you start, you have to either open, open a particular observation or do a search and open it through that.
Does that make sense?
Um, the transcription box has got a summarize button, which doesn't do anything yet. Um, now, I wonder how we want to do, you know, we want a pop-up window with a speaker characterization?

Um, either we could do that, you know, when does the pop-up come? Either we can, when you click on the, the ID, any sort of ID in the transcription box, or we can put an extra button, extra few buttons next to the summarize button, so that you, actually in the transcription box, but so that you click on a button and then it opens whatever that speaker characterization is. The problem is, the, the left click is already used because it highlights that, um, that part speech or whatever that, what he's going to say.
The left click.

The left click highlights it. So that you can, I don't know what happens when you do it on a window, actually. But that would be a bit annoying if you have a left click for one thing and double click for something else.
Um, I think, so yeah, when you left click it, you can, for example, set, set the marker there so that the, the audio goes from there, I think.
Um, so we can't put it on left click. We could put it on the right click. We could, for example, have a little menu that pops up.
Yeah, that would be quite good, I suppose.
So, right click on the menu, you know, and you can click on speaker characterization on the top, so, you know.
What else could we have in the menu?
That's a good point. I don't know.
So, otherwise, it's just on the right click.
Yeah, yeah, but, um, I don't know about you, but usually in Windows, the right click doesn't do anything, does it? It opens a menu.
A menu, yeah. Yeah, that's what I mean, I think. So, it might be a bit weird for it to just start bringing up stuff in there.
To just have sort of the same sort of video throughout.
Yeah.
Yeah.
Um, or just, you know, or just a button.
I guess a button, button makes a bit more sense because otherwise you don't really know that, oh, what if I right click now, what happens then?
Well, no, no, you still have the menu, the menu pop-up that, well, oh, yeah, it's more obvious, isn't it?
It's more already agreed, isn't it? It's got a button.
Yeah, that's true, yeah, it's more intuitive.
Well, then it's not as accessible. Like, if you want to add more things in the future, you might, you know, need buttons.
Having a worse menu.
Maybe.
More flexible.
Yeah, well, I mean, it.
